hints.title: Consecutive Day Threshold Island Detection
hints.text: Peak attendance records must span three or more contiguous calendar identifiers where headcount reaches or exceeds one hundred.

hints.title: Contiguity Grouping via Row Number Offset
hints.text: Filter entries with people >= 100. Subtract row_number() over (order by id) from id to assign contiguous sequences to an identical grouping key.

hints.title: Common Table Expression Island Blueprint
hints.text: Construct a CTE with id - row_number() over (order by id) as grp. Join with a subquery filtering for group sizes >= 3, and order by id.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
WITH HighTraffic AS (
    SELECT id, visit_date, people,
           id - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY id) AS grp
    FROM Stadium
    WHERE people >= 100
),
GroupCounts AS (
    SELECT grp, COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM HighTraffic
    GROUP BY grp
    HAVING cnt >= 3
)
SELECT h.id, h.visit_date, h.people
FROM HighTraffic h
JOIN GroupCounts g ON h.grp = g.grp
ORDER BY h.id;
```

complexity.notes: Window function row number assignment followed by group size filtering.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Three-way self-joins take cubic O(S^3) time without indexes and miss islands longer than 3 days without duplicate handling.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Gaps-and-islands window grouping isolates contiguous runs in a single sorting pass.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Proficiency with gaps-and-islands logic using ROW_NUMBER() difference technique.
